clauses.current_legal_basis: Operative predicate: the designation of the African Development Bank as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act under this order is listed in a note to 22 U.S.C. 288 in the held U.S. Code release point 119-121 and in 8 CFR 316.20 in the held eCFR text current through 2026-10-14 (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/cfr-t8-316.20.txt, which cites E.O. 12403, Feb. 8, 1983); no held instrument revokes it.
clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Section 1 designates the African Development Bank as a public international organization entitled to the privileges, exemptions and immunities of the International Organizations Immunities Act, with a rule that the designation does not abridge privileges the Bank has acquired by treaty or congressional action and does not affect the Agreement's Article 52 section 1, Article 57 or the Article 64 declaration. It has no end date or condition; the number search of the held texts finds it still listed in 8 CFR 316.20 (eCFR current through 2026-10-14) and in a note to 22 U.S.C. 288, and none of the later orders in the packet touches section 1.

clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Section 2 amends EO 11269 in sections 2(c), 3(d) and 7 by adding the African Development Bank to the list that already named the African Development Fund. Under the 2026-10-21 strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues, amended, while the parent order continues. EO 12567, EO 12647 and EO 12766 each struck the end of the list and re-inserted it with the African Development Bank kept and a new institution added (before and after: the list grows, the Bank stays); EO 13118 amended section 7's heading and opening words and sections 1(b) and 4(a) for agency changes, not the list. EO 11269 as amended is still printed as a note to 22 U.S.C. 286b and that note's status line lists this order, so the amendment was not ended.

clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Section 3 delegates to the Secretary of the Treasury the functions vested in the President by sections 1333(c), 1334, 1338(a) and 1341(b) of Public Law 97-35 (22 U.S.C. 290i-1(c), 290i-2, 290i-6(a), 290i-9(b)). It has no end date or condition and the held U.S. Code carries a delegation note under each of those four sections referring to this order, so the delegation was still recorded as in force; no held instrument amends or revokes it.

research_rationale:
EO 12403 (signed 1983-02-08, Ronald Reagan; 48 FR 6087, printed in the Federal Register of 1983-02-10) has three operative sections: section 1 designates the African Development Bank under the International Organizations Immunities Act, section 2 amends EO 11269 sections 2(c), 3(d) and 7 to add the Bank to the lists of institutions, and section 3 delegates to the Secretary of the Treasury the President's functions under four sections of Public Law 97-35. I read the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12403.txt in full (identity matches the register: number, title, date, signer, FR page) and the three prepared inventory clauses cover every operative section; the preamble recitals and the editorial note are not operative. The order states no duration, condition or separate effective date, so it took effect on signing. Later orders found by the number search and the chain: EO 12567, EO 12647 and EO 12766 successively amend the same lists in EO 11269 (strike-and-insert; the Bank stays in each list) and EO 13118 amends EO 11269 section 7's heading and opening words; none revokes EO 12403 or removes the Bank. The U.S. Code search (release point 119-121 current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected) found the designation listed in a note to 22 U.S.C. 288, the delegation notes under 22 U.S.C. 290i-1, 290i-2, 290i-6 and 290i-9, and EO 11269 as amended by this order in a note to 22 U.S.C. 286b; the eCFR search (as of 2026-10-14) found 8 CFR 316.20 listing the Bank with the citation E.O. 12403. The Federal Register disposition-note search returned no note for this order. All three clauses are operative.

savings.reason: The order has no savings or transition clause; the privileges and immunities in section 1 are expressly not abridged as to those the Bank acquired by treaty or congressional action, which is a limit written into the continuing designation rather than a separate surviving effect.
